Which version of a document applies when a reference is specific?
Only the cited version applies.
How is the applicable version determined for non-specific references?
The latest version of the referenced document, including any amendments, applies.
What are intermodulation products?
Intermodulation products are unwanted signals generated when two or more signals are present in a non-linear circuit.
How does the OSI reference model address the requirements for data arrival and data usability?

It defines network protocol operation in terms of lower level network services to ensure data arrives correctly and in a timely manner, and higher level protocols to ensure data is recognizable and in the proper form for correct use.
How many functional layers does the OSI reference model identify?
The OSI reference model identifies seven functional layers.
Which layers of the OSI model does the TETRA standard define protocols for?
The TETRA standard defines the protocols up to layer 3 of the OSI model.
What is TEDS and which TETRA standard version first incorporated it?
TEDS stands for TETRA Enhanced Data Service, also known as High-Speed Data (HSD). It was first incorporated in the TETRA standard ETSI EN 300 392-2 V3.2.1.
What change regarding control channels was introduced in TETRA standard version V3.5.1?
Version V3.5.1 added an alternative option called Direct Access, which allows cells to use a QAM HSD channel as the main control channel.
Which propagation models are specified in the system assumptions?
The specified propagation models are TU50-400 MHz, HT200-800 MHz, and static.
In TETRA standard ETSI EN 300 392-2 V3.4.1 and earlier versions, what channel is assigned to an MS that did not negotiate QoS and did not specifically request a phase modulation channel?
The MS is assigned to a single-slot π/4-DQPSK PDCH.

How does the SwMI choose a PDCH in more recent versions of ETSI EN 300 392-2 if the MS did not negotiate QoS during PDP context activation and does not specifically request a phase modulation channel?

The SwMI chooses a PDCH based on the MS’s declared capabilities and the default assumption that the PDP context is required for background class data with unspecified throughput, delay and reliability.
What is the maximum number of independent unacknowledged advanced links an MS may have per group address in the current version of ETSI EN 300 392-2?
In the current version of ETSI EN 300 392-2, the MS may have up to four independent unacknowledged advanced links per group address.
When does the calculation using ERP and conversion factors fail, requiring direct observations of the main carrier's signal level?
The calculation fails near the azimuthal edge of a sectored channel, so the MS has to make direct observations of the main carrier's signal level when using a failing sectored channel.
What causes inter-modulation products in a transmitter and how are they controlled?

Inter-modulation products are components generated by transmitter non-linearity when an interfering signal reaching via the antenna is present together with the wanted signal. Limits are introduced in the standard to inhibit the generation of such components.
What does the symbol $E_{m}(k)$ represent in the context of transmitter signal modeling?
$E_{m}(k)$ represents the complex-valued (vector) error associated with the symbol $S_{m}(k)$, which is caused by transmitter inaccuracies.
What are the two main components into which the modified Hata model divides total path loss (PL)?
The two main components are median loss (L_m) and loss due to slow fading (L_s).
How is the link propagation model represented in TETRA channel performance simulations?
It is represented by a stationary complex tap-gain process, described in terms of Probability Density Function (PDF) and a Power Density Spectrum (PDS) which models the Doppler spectrum.
Which channel model is used for high-speed data QAM channel simulations to improve accuracy, particularly under the HT200 propagation environment?
The GSM six-tap model (table 8.30) is used.
What are the statistical properties of the real and imaginary parts of the tap-gain process a(t) in the CLASS model?
The real and imaginary parts exhibit an identical Gaussian PDF, an identical PDS, and are mutually statistically independent.
What are the main assumptions regarding signal bandwidth, modulation and coding rate combinations, and channel models in the simulation scenario?

How are time-varying path gains modeled in terms of their statistical properties and power spectrum?

How is polynomial interpolation used in the described method, and what property of matrix H allows for simplification of the matrix inversion?

What physical phenomena constitute the dispersive multipath model describing radio wave propagation in the mobile radio environment?

How are TETRA propagation models derived from GSM tapped delay line models?
TETRA adopts the GSM models in principle but uses a reduced number of taps (paths) to account for the much smaller system bandwidth of TETRA.
What are the four defining characteristics of the propagation models specified in the TETRA standard?

How is Rician fading achieved in the propagation model typical for flat rural areas?

Rician fading is achieved by applying a tap-gain process (RICE) which is the sum of a complex component (STATIC(fs)) with a constant magnitude and a constant Doppler shift fs, and a complex random component (CLASS) with a Rayleigh distributed magnitude and a power density spectrum according to the classical Doppler spectrum.
For which types of environments is the Hata model used in this ETR to estimate path loss?

How is spectrum access coordinated in licensed bands with exclusive access?

In licensed bands with exclusive access, the regulator coordinates frequency access. One licensee operates on a particular frequency or band and is provided with interference protection rights by the regulator, while no other licensees are permitted access to that spectrum.
What role does the regulator play when interference arises between users in exclusive licensed bands?
The regulator becomes involved if interference between users cannot be resolved by the operators themselves.
What are the characteristics of non-exclusive licensed bands regarding fees and interference management?
